title: Runahead prefetch orchestration and KV-slab rebalance for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Asha Nair
description: Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (short user prompts interleaved with long assistant responses) cause uneven KV residency and GPU memory fragmentation. Continuous batching currently prioritizes immediate coalescing which increases tail latency for long-turn responses and yields poor GPU heap utilization during sustained bursts. Goals: (1) Design a runahead prefetch orchestration layer that issues KV prefetches for predicted upcoming slots to reduce cache miss latency for long responses without amplifying peak memory, (2) Implement a KV-slab rebalance that classifies hot/cold KV pages to enable selective compaction and reduce fragmentation, (3) Integrate priority-aware slot pinning so high-SLO requests can reserve lightweight KV footholds, (4) Validate end-to-end on Redwood Dedicated workloads and roll out to hosted after telemetry shows improvements. Success metrics: p95 latency decrease >=10% on mixed-dialogue benchmark, average GPU memory fragmentation reduction >=15%, no more than 3% throughput regression on peak QPS. Constraints: must not increase tail memory usage beyond current SLA allowance, and must be compatible with on-prem (no privileged kernel changes).
comments: 2026-02-19 — Kickoff: scoped design doc and experiments. Attendees: Miguel, Asha, Priya, Lena. Action: prototype runahead predictor and small synthetic harness (ref: confluence link)

2026-02-24 — Spike complete: implemented horizon predictor using exponential moving average of token counts per slot. Early result: predictor hits 88% recall for 5-token horizon on our mixed-dialogue replay; chosen for low overhead.

2026-03-02 — Benchmarks: baseline (no prefetch) vs prefetch-only vs prefetch+slab rebalance on g4dn-like hosts. Observed -9% p95, -6% p99 with prefetch; combined approach gave -13% p95 and -10% p99. Fragmentation metric (CUDA mempool free-slab ratio) improved ~18%.

2026-03-04 — Found regression: under extreme short-burst traffic prefetch increased KV residency, causing minor OOM events on smaller Dedicated instances. Mitigation: implement ephemeral pinning with time-to-live tied to request priority to avoid long-term memory growth.

2026-03-06 — Design review notes: PM request to add feature flag gate and rollout plan. Security said no additional review needed. UX: console needs a telemetry toggle for ‘prefetch horizon’ and ‘slab-compaction’ metrics. Documented in confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Runahead+Prefetch+Design

2026-03-09 — PR opened for prototype runtime changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4286 — includes predictor, prefetch queue, and slab classifier hooks. Linked integration test PR for mempool safety: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tests/pull/981

2026-03-11 — Load test on Dedicated staging: canary 5% traffic for 24h. Result: p95 down 12.3% on mixed workload, memory fragmentation down 19.1%, CPU overhead +2.1%. No incidents. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Batching/Runahead-prefetch-canary

2026-03-12 — Retrospective notes & next steps: stabilize ephemeral pin TTL heuristics, add adaptive horizon based on observed slot variance, implement proactive slab compaction scheduler to run in low-util windows, and prepare rollout plan for hosted API with feature flag and telemetry gate. Assigned follow-ups: ENG-893345 (TTL tuning), ENG-893346 (adaptive horizon), ENG-893347 (compaction scheduler).
